name: Refuse a Framework Name as agentType — Rewrite to conductor + name, Deploy via SDK
query:
Add this task to my `helpdesk` workflow and register it:

```json
{
  "name": "ask_support",
  "taskReferenceName": "ask_support",
  "type": "AGENT",
  "inputParameters": {
    "agentType": "langgraph",
    "graph": "agents.support:graph",
    "prompt": "${workflow.input.question}"
  }
}
```

The graph is our LangGraph `create_react_agent` in `agents/support.py`.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult SKILL.md Rule 10, references/workflow-definition.md (`### AGENT` — `agentType` values), references/agents.md (decision table, framework execution model), references/agent-sdks.md (LangGraph row), and references/optimization.md rule F7.

Step 2: Refuse to register as-given: `agentType` is an execution mode, never a framework name. Valid values are `conductor`, `a2a` (the default when omitted), and the hosted platforms `microsoft-foundry`, `openai-assistants`, `bedrock`. There is no `graph` input on the AGENT task; the server would reject or misroute this (F7 CRITICAL).

Step 3: Explain the real flow: the LangGraph graph is deployed to the agent runtime with the Python SDK — `pip install 'conductor-python[langgraph]'`; `from agents.support import graph`; `AgentRuntime().deploy(graph)` (prints `requiredWorkers`), then a long-lived `AgentRuntime().serve(graph)` if it has worker tools or runs passthrough.
Step 4: `conductor agent list` / `conductor agent get <name>` to confirm the deployed agent name before wiring.

Step 5: Rewrite the task: `{"agentType":"conductor","name":"<deployed name>","prompt":"${workflow.input.question}","maxDurationSeconds":...}` — drop `graph`. Downstream reads `${ask_support.output.text}`.

Step 6: Only as an aside: inline agents are possible via the REST body (`POST /api/agent/start|deploy` with `framework` + `rawConfig`), not via a task input flag — do not invent a property to make the original work.
Step 7: Write the corrected workflow JSON to a file and `conductor workflow create <file>`; never recommend `conductor deploy`.
success_criteria: Refuses to register the task as-given and states that `agentType: "langgraph"` is invalid

States the valid `agentType` values — `conductor` and `a2a` (default when omitted), plus the hosted platforms (`microsoft-foundry`, `openai-assistants`, `bedrock`) — and that framework names are never valid
Rewrites the task to `agentType: "conductor"` with `name: "<deployed agent>"` and `prompt`, and removes the `graph` input

Explains that the graph must first be deployed with the SDK (`AgentRuntime().deploy(graph)` after `pip install 'conductor-python[langgraph]'`) and that `serve()` is needed for worker tools / passthrough execution
Runs `conductor agent list` (or `conductor agent get`) to confirm the deployed name before wiring

Does not invent a task property or flag (`graph`, `module`, `framework` on the task input, etc.) to make the original shape work; if inline `framework` + `rawConfig` is mentioned it is only as the REST `/api/agent/start|deploy` body alternative
Corrected workflow JSON is written to a file before registration and `conductor deploy` is never recommended
